verdict: Area has unusually principled foundations and uneven execution on top of them. Padding is computed from the capital height and the icon box, so text in Button, Chip, Segmented, Menu, Checkbox and Radio sits exactly centred on every tile; corners nest concentrically by rule; inks are solved for every ground under every setting; state fills keep their order; and overlays use the platform's top layer with motion fully tokenised. None of the fifteen published systems or six live products read derives padding, corners and inks this way.

The weakness is uniformity, not taste, and it has six root causes. First, the defaults moved (type 14 to 13, corner 8 to 10) without the formulas and comments written for them, so values land between rungs: a 10 px row gap, a corner step of 10 px beside an 8 px medium control, a 17 px code line, an 11 px corner. Second, families built in different sessions restate the same part (frame, row, field shell, header bar, mark, popup surface) with small differences, so seven card corners and four mark heights render side by side. Third, behaviour is written per family (five menu engines, five typeaheads, three focus models) and tested in none.

Fourth, against shipped products Area is out of range in one direction: overlay motion about twice as long, floating lists roomier and rounder, dark washes two to three times heavier, one text ink fewer than the desktop apps, and dark muted text only 1.49:1 from the default. Fifth, hierarchy is flat: nothing goes above 20/28 or weight 500, while every product measured titles pages at 590–700. Sixth, nothing rendered is tested, so drift returns after every pass, and the gallery's own faults (broken tile names, stages wider than their cards, demos that hide their state) make good components look unfinished.

Done looks like this: each shared part is one recipe that every family reads; each rule has a rendered check that fails when a value drifts, and each shared behaviour a browser test; the owner's choices on motion, menu density, corners, washes and inks are made from the evidence; the heading weight and large title are adopted; and every family scores at least 4 on balance, spacing, type, shape, colour and feel, light and dark, in a fresh capture at the new defaults.
strengths: Padding derived from the capital height and the icon box, with the border counted once and whole pixels, centres text exactly in Button, Chip, Segmented, Menu, Nav, Command palette, List box, Checkbox and Radio.
Concentric corners are a stated rule (the outer corner less the inset, with a floor), stricter than the component libraries read; Board's 16 / 8 / 8 px nesting is exact.
Inks are solved for each ground under every setting, and state fills keep their order (hover, then selected, then pressed), which no other system guarantees in code.
Every derived token re-derives inside a scoped subtree, and Pills is set per family.
In light, Area's text hierarchy sits exactly at the live products' median: muted is 5.74:1, and its step from the default is 2.57 against a median of 2.6.
Overlays use the native popover and modal dialog, motion is tokens with no literal durations, and exits are tested to be faster than entries.
Tooltip handling (a skip window, name tooltips that let the pointer pass, closing when the window loses focus) goes beyond what the component libraries read ship.
Type and density are separate numbers, with 63 settings that keep their inks solved.
Copy button, Abbreviation, Radio, Segmented, Button, Board, Breadcrumb, Timeline, Plan, Menu and Command palette already read as shipped product, named independently by four reviewers.

scores.why: The median family scores 4, and Button, Menu, Command palette, Board, Plan and Timeline read as shipped product. Faint light plates and roomy, round floating lists hold it back.
One manifest, a parity check and an independent settings registry are rare. But six list box implementations share no keyboard hook, there is no frame part, and slots are spelled five ways.
Text is exactly centred in Button, Menu and Checkbox but 0.6 px high in a dozen families; Switch sits 3 px high in Setting row, Panel's rows use two grids, and templates leave 79 px empty.
Card-like frames use seven corners, marks four heights and three corner rules, header bars about eight heights, and open triggers five different looks.
Card and Surface share a corner but not inset or title, chat cards use eight corners, and rows agree on height and paint but not on corner, edge or icon ink.
Toasts render unusable under modals, required pickers submit empty, and 11 families have targets under 24 px with no hit expansion.
Tooltip handling and Combobox match or beat the libraries read, but submenus close on the way to them, menus run on five engines, and overlays take about twice the references' time.
Motion is tokens end to end and every hover is gated to devices that hover, but literal fills remain, about 25 comments quote stale numbers, and style files are not named by family.
Two text inks where the desktop apps use three or four, dark muted text only 1.49:1 from the default, and a hierarchy that stops at 20/28 and 500.
63 settings with solved inks per ground, ordered state fills and scoped re-derivation, which no reference has; but there is no typeface setting, and the second and third brand colours reach nothing.
A 3.4 MB unminified stylesheet in one file, no memoised rows or windowed lists anywhere, and layout reads on every scroll in every menu.
No shipped compositions, so every product recreation rebuilt the shell; no responsive or safe-area rules; and mobile, media and calendar are the weakest product types.

rules.topic: Small gaps and the gap ladder
rules.rule: A gap takes whole density steps and lands on the ladder 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 px; only an inset (edge to content) keeps the half step. Between siblings there are three roles: a joined set 2 px, actions in a header or a line of text 4 px, and independent controls 6, 8 or 10 px by density. Inside a mark, gaps are 2 or 4 px.
rules.today: At type 13 the half step is 0.5, so the row gap is 10 px, Card's section gaps 14 and 18 px, Tabs 18 and 14 px, Stack's section 20 px, Description list's row gap 2 px and Card's carousel 7 px, values on no ladder. Page header actions, Drawer's stacked footer and the toast list are a fixed 8 px, and Badge's label gaps are 1, 3 and 4 px.
rules.gap: About a dozen gaps are 2 px off their rung at Default. The row gap is the exception: moving it to its rung (12 px) would make menus roomier, away from every reference, so it is decided first.

rules.rule: A line joined to a name in the same box is the name's size in the muted ink; the smaller size is for text set apart from what it explains. A title and its copy are 4 px apart on compact surfaces. A text list is its line plus 4 px and a key-value list its line plus 8 px; a metadata line in a row keeps the row's 18 px line; and code leading follows the type setting (16 px at type 13, never 17).
rules.today: Joined lines are 12 px in eleven families and 13 px in eight more, so a Switch is 13 over 12 while the same setting in a Setting row is 13 over 13. Reference list, Link groups and Description list rows sit 18, 22 and 26 px apart. Code block small and Diff run 11 px on a 17 px line, and Field's count sits about 1 px off its description's baseline.
rules.gap: The direction of joined lines, the two list rhythms, the code leading and the misuse of the smallest size. The live products set title to description at 8 px where Area uses 4; that is an option within the joined-lines decision, since the owner set 4 on 2026-11-06.

rules.topic: When type size changes and when ink changes
rules.rule: Size steps between levels: page 24, section 16, item 13, with titles from title-sm up at 600. Inside a level, ink or weight steps, never both, except a surface title over its copy. The 11 px size is only for marks, a mark's text follows its size prop and never density, tone colours the mark and never the words, and weight rises only with the default ink (except control labels that keep one weight in every state, and the 500 muted group label).
rules.today: Twelve word parts are set at 11 px. Tag's text changes with density (13 px at Default, 11 at Compact). Alert's title and Tabs' change labels are in tone ink, there are four group-heading treatments, item names split between 500 and 400, and nothing goes above 20 px or 500.
rules.gap: The heading hierarchy, the smallest-size rule, joined lines, group headings, one weight table, tone on marks, and Tag's text.

rules.rule: Every one-line label or value in a control, row or tab is centred on its capitals: a trimmed span, or a native input offset by the same amount. Multi-line content aligns to its first line by a box one first line tall. A ghost icon action at an edge puts its glyph on the text column, and the first label in a strip sits on the content column.
rules.today: Half the system centres exactly; field values, Switch, Tabs, Tree view, Pagination, Panel rows and Tooltip sit 0.6 px high. Switch sits 3 px high in Setting row, Menu's two-line rows centre their leading icon, Card's and Message's ghost actions sit 7 px inside the column, and plate Tabs do not hang their plate.
rules.gap: One centring model, the two-line icon decision, a control keeping its row's centre, edge ghost buttons, and the navigation round.

rules.rule: The Corner number is the real medium control's corner, and every full-width row takes its own height's corner. A surface steps off the controls it holds by a stated amount, and a resting card is never rounder than the floating surface over it. A nested shape is the outer corner less the inset, with a floor at the 8 px row corner; a corner control is concentric and equidistant from both edges; and components read only public corner roles.
rules.today: The corner step is computed for a 32 px box (10 px) while the 30 px medium control draws 8, so floating-list rows are 10 px beside Nav rows at 8. Card is 18 px, Asset card 20, Design card 24 and Dialog 20. Dialog's close is 3 px off concentric, Toast's and Alert's 3, Popover's 1, Calendar's 2 and Queue's row actions 2, while Tooltip's Kbd is exact; Card's well and Surface inside Panel nest at 4 px, and File upload reads a raw setting value.
rules.gap: Two fixes to the corner step and the public roles, the owner's corner decision, the corner-control rule, and the nested floor in the shared frame.

rules.rule: A text side is the height less the capital height, halved, less the border, rounded, plus the border; an icon side is the height less the icon, halved. The border is counted once and the result is a whole pixel. Pill-shaped fields, Buttons and Chips add room for the curve (the corner less 3/8 of the height), and marks use (height − 6) / 2.
rules.today: The formula holds in every control family; rendered sides of 10, 7, 8 and 14 px at small to large are exact. Six centred slots skip the rounding (10.38 px), floating lists pad 4 px inside their border so rows sit 5 px from the outer edge (documented), Tag's side is 5 px, Kbd's 4 and Citation's 7 where the mark rule gives 6, and pill Buttons keep a rectangle's sides.
rules.gap: Whole-pixel insets, the floating-list border decision, one mark, and pill side room. Fields place text at 0.33 of their height where three products use 0.375–0.41; that is kept, because it would break the shared start with Button.

rules.rule: A container spaces its children by its gap; a pair that joins is its own group, never a margin that undoes the parent's gap. Section and page spaces are named roles, and a surface's gap between blocks is never larger than its inset.
rules.today: Eight margins subtract the parent's gap, Stack doubles the row gap for a section with no token, and Popover's blocks are 14 px apart inside a 12 px edge.
rules.gap: Children spaced by gap, named section and page spaces, and the block-gap rule.

rules.rule: A nested backplate (Kbd, Badge, Count, an input action, steppers, a chip's remove) reserves its own square box. A control inside a row keeps the row's height and is centred in its own target, growing its hit area invisibly. An inline chip never exceeds its line, and an unpainted region takes no inset of its own.
rules.today: The nested boxes are right. Table's checkbox column makes rows 44 px instead of 39, Mention chips are 21 px tall in an 18 px line, inline Code's box is 21.38 px, and a soft Surface pads 14 px while painting nothing (to be measured again at the new light default).
rules.gap: A control in a row, one mark, the code type sizes, and the shared frame.

rules.rule: Text is placed on its glyphs (capital and baseline, trimmed). Marks share one whole-pixel capital baseline, a text-only card looks even at top and bottom, dark weights may need lowering to offset glow, and a list highlight lands and leaves at once.
rules.today: Trimming is applied in 26 files and the marks' baseline holds. Card's last line is trimmed to its descent, leaving 4–5 px more below the text than above it (a recorded rule). There is no dark weight offset, and Menu row plates fade and trail the pointer.
rules.gap: The card bottom and dark weight decisions, and the instant list highlight.

rules.rule: Joined controls sit 2 px apart (segments, row actions), header actions 4 px, independent controls 6–10 px by density, and footer buttons 8 px at Default. Every interactive box has a 24 px target, 44 px under a coarse pointer, and a seam inside a joined control reads the control edge.
rules.today: Four values with no stated roles, eleven families with targets under 24 px and no expansion (Split button's icon trigger is 15 px wide), and Input group's seams lighter than its own edge.
rules.gap: The three gap roles, the shared hit target, and the field shell.

phases.title: Safety net and truth
phases.summary: The other worktree is merged first, then the capture tools become a rendered check, browser tests arrive, the gallery's faults are fixed, and the status registry, API tab and stale docs are corrected. The published data, vocabulary, file structure and release work can trail.
phases.ends: “The gallery as it really is”: every family captured again at the merged defaults (light Layers 50), the baseline every later page compares against. The menu density question is also asked here.

phases.title: Foundations
phases.summary: The decisions come first so no value is tuned twice: heights, menu density, corners, the third ink, dark washes, overlay motion, dark elevation and joined lines. Then the derivations: gaps, corners, inks, motion, focus, dark edges, heights, type, plates and pixels.
phases.ends: “Foundations”: a Menu over a Card over the page, a form row, a toolbar, a page header and a chat column, at Compact, Default and Comfortable, light and dark.

phases.title: Shared parts
phases.summary: Each repeated part becomes one recipe: the frame, the row, the field shell, the header bar and corner control, marks, the popup surface, state paint, and twins and density. Every family that uses a part reads it.
phases.ends: “One recipe per part”: grouped by part, with every family that changed listed under it.

phases.title: Behaviour
phases.summary: The browser tests must pass first. Then the shared hooks (timing, list navigation, menus, focus movement, forms, overlays) are adopted family by family, and performance follows.
phases.ends: Recordings, not stills: a submenu reached diagonally, a toast over a dialog, a form reset, plus the stylesheet size before and after.

phases.title: Family defects
phases.summary: One round per kind: navigation, content, conversation and fields. The carried writing decisions and the app audit's gaps close the phase.
phases.ends: A short page for each round.

phases.title: Capabilities
phases.summary: Each new capability goes through the intake ladder as a proposal before it is built. The app shell and the thread come first, because they unblock the product recreations.
phases.ends: Each proposal on its own page, built only at the owner's request.

workstreams.title: Foundations recalibrated
workstreams.summary: Gaps, corners, inks, washes, motion, focus, dark elevation, heights, type, plates and pixel rounding, carried to the new defaults and checked against the references.

workstreams.title: Shared parts
workstreams.summary: One recipe each for the frame, row, field shell, header bar, mark, popup surface and state paint, so families stop restating them.

workstreams.title: Behaviour engine
workstreams.summary: One menu engine, one list navigation and typeahead, one focus model, form participation, overlay fixes, timing in one place, and performance and delivery.

workstreams.title: Family defects
workstreams.summary: The remaining defects of single families, in one round per kind, plus carried decisions and the app audit's gaps.

workstreams.title: Capabilities and coverage
workstreams.summary: The app shell, thread, grids, responsive and touch rules, scroll fades, drag and drop, customization gaps and the variants the reviews named, each through intake.

workstreams.title: Truth and safety net
workstreams.summary: Merge the built work, make rendering and behaviour testable, fix the gallery and the docs, and publish rules and measurements as data.

items.title: Merge the other worktree's built work first
items.what: Another worktree holds finished, uncommitted work: a heading weight of 600 and extra-large title tokens that no component reads yet, the light Layer contrast default moved from 0 to 50 (dark stays 0), a darkest light ground of #f1f3f5, adjusted chart grounds and danger colour, and Link as a button. Every light ground, plate and well in this evaluation's captures was rendered before that change, at Layers 0.
items.change: The owner commits that branch, it is merged and rebuilt, and the gallery is captured again at the new default. The light findings that depend on the ground (faint plates and wells, the soft Surface, region depth) are measured again before anything is tuned.
items.why: Built work is merged, never redone, and nothing in the foundations is tuned on old values. The work was confirmed by reading that worktree.
items.risk: It conflicts only with this worktree's research files.

items.title: Rendered checks from the capture tools
items.what: Nothing checks Area as rendered: there are no screenshot baselines and no accessibility, target-size, right-to-left or forced-colours runs. The capture set this evaluation measured (1,371 tiles, 27,441 elements) was temporary and is already gone.
items.change: The capture tools move into the repository and become a rendered check that measures the gallery at the defaults, light and dark, and fails when a rule drifts: text centred within 0.1 px in control boxes, nothing painting outside its card, header bars at the two set heights, marks 14, 18 and 22 px tall, one edge on a dark floating surface. Review pages gain baseline pictures, and the first-position check for Tabs and Segmented and the Compact small marks are added.
items.why: Every visible rule the plan writes needs a check, or drift returns after each pass. The rendered review found many values that had moved since they were set.
items.risk: The capture browser is a different engine version from the app's, so checks compare lengths in CSS px, never pixel differences.

items.title: Behaviour tests in a real browser
items.what: No package has a DOM or browser test tool, and arrow keys are handled in 21 files that no test covers.
items.change: Component tests run in a real browser against the built gallery. The first suites cover menu keys and typeahead, focus moving through lists, form reset and required fields, modal focus and dismissal, and hit targets.
items.why: Behaviour that a shared hook owns is tested once, and every family that adopts the hook inherits the test. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Tile names keep their spaces and parentheses
items.what: The gallery splits a tile's name only where a lowercase letter meets a capital, so “inADialog” reads “In adialog” and “List (default)” reads “List default)”. 17 tiles in 15 families show broken names.
items.change: Names also split before a capital that starts a word, a specimen's own title is used when it has one, and a test reads every label.
items.why: A tile name is read as words, and a broken one makes a finished component look unfinished. Seen in the render and confirmed in source.

items.title: Gallery stages stay inside their cards
items.what: Every Chart tile, seven Description list tiles and every Shortcut list and Meter tile run wider than their card (385 px in a 388 px view), so first letters and legend keys clip. Input group's field collapses to 0 × 18 px in 9 of 12 tiles and the vertical Slider's track is 0 px tall, because the gallery sets a full-width field inside a stage that shrinks to its content; Pagination, File upload and Splitter tiles crowd or overrun their cards.
items.change: Wide demos get one-column cards, fluid demos take the stage's width, and group demos are full width. In the components, a grouped field never shrinks below its content, and a vertical Slider reads its own length (16 rem) with a floor of the thumb plus twice the track inset.
items.why: A gallery stage never runs wider than its card, and a component never borrows a width setting for a length. Measured on every affected tile.
items.risk: The Slider length is a hook, not a size, and is recorded with the other width hooks.

items.title: Demos show the state they name
items.what: The floating Toolbar sits at opacity 0, Tree view's Guides tile matches Small, Nav's picture tile is blank under a white sticky heading, Hover card is never open and Reference list's Highlighted shows nothing. Tiles meant to wrap (Figure, Board, Section heading, Editable text, Message) render one line and Alert's multiline tile shrinks to 100 px. Smaller slips: Message authors never share a column, Toast tones sit under Content, Badge group shows a stray grip, Avatar group mixes circles and squares, and Badge tiles are lowercase beside Badge group's title case.
items.change: Demos force their state, wrap demos get fixed widths, and gallery tests fail when a text meant to wrap stays on one line or a specimen is invisible.
items.why: No specimen is invisible at rest, a state tile shows its state, and a wrap tile wraps at the default type. Seen in the render.
items.risk: Nothing changes in the components.

items.title: Demo copy and pictures that read as product
items.what: The phone Input reads “+1 1”, Combobox shows the word “Placeholder”, the new Password field has no placeholder, and Chip, Popover and Attachment show a checkerboard “Image”. Every Tag picker tag is a different hue, overlays read Title / Description / Action in 472 px tall tiles, the stat and weather templates leave 79 px empty, and the whole gallery has two pictures.
items.change: A copy pass in the placeholder vocabulary with realistic values, and one shared picture set: six to eight neutral photos at several ratios, three screenshots of Area and one portrait of David Tee. Tag picker's default is neutral, and template squares hug their content or carry a small Chart.
items.why: Demos are judged as product, so they use realistic words and one picture set, with plates only in loading states. Seen in the render; medium confidence because part of it is taste.
items.risk: Pictures must be Area's own screenshots or photos the owner holds.

items.title: No family shows as Unrefined by accident
items.what: Code block, Composer, Custom select and Meter show as Unrefined although their notes say In review. Why a family is in review lives in one 2,000-character comment, and pages show no stage date.
items.change: The four are listed as In review, each review stage carries a date, a reason and a source shown on the family's page, and a test checks every page's status.
items.why: A family's status is data, not a comment, so it cannot be mislabelled silently. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Completion stays the owner's to confirm; this only stops the mislabel.

items.title: API tab and prop types generated from the manifest
items.what: The API tab is written by hand and is wrong in at least 14 families: Alert and Toast list 5 of their 7 tones, Toast shows a retired action, Badge lacks Plain, Button lists 8 tones and Dialog has no size. 17 React prop types are typed by hand (four with values the manifest lacks), two families have a size with no axis, 25 axes in 18 families have no default, and loading is spelled four different ways.
items.change: The API tab is generated from the manifest and the props' own documentation, every visual prop's type comes from the manifest, single-value axes become on/off props or state their default, and a check makes every behaviour prop match a manifest state.
items.why: The manifest is the one source for variants and props, and nothing restates it. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Type changes can break the app's own uses, so old names stay as aliases for one release.

items.title: Stale comments, counts and rule tables
items.what: About 25 comments and doc lines quote numbers that no longer render at the defaults, such as a label column of 36 px that is 34 px and “12 + 4 = 16” where the code computes 20. The architecture counts are stale (99 / 138 / 119 / 7 against a real 108 / 150 / 126 / 10), the Strokes and Elevation tables name tokens nothing reads, the components list still names Preview frame, the weight exceptions are unwritten, and one census files Toggletip with Popover though it uses Tooltip's bubble.
items.change: Every line is corrected, the Strokes table and the counts are generated, a lint flags any line that quotes a number “at the default”, and the foundation-change skill gains a step that sweeps such comments when a ramp or default changes.
items.why: A comment quotes a formula, or the value at the shipped defaults (type 13, density 32, corner 10). Confirmed line by line in source.

items.title: Each family's measurements and rules published as data
items.what: Usage entries have six fields: 70 of 126 list no states and 33 no keys. No page gives a family's measurements, token rules live in prose and comments, and there is no table an author can use to pair inks with grounds.
items.change: Each family page gains a Specs tab generated from the tokens (height, sides with and without an icon, gap, corner, icon size, type role, tokens per state) at the current settings and the defaults. Public tokens carry their usage and rules for Area's check and assistant tools, a generated table says which inks reach 4.5:1 and 3:1 on which grounds, usage entries are filled in, and a writing skill is made from the writing guide.
items.why: The published systems read print their measurements and rules; Area already computes them but shows none.
items.risk: The Specs tab must evaluate the same calculations the CSS does.

items.title: One vocabulary for parts, states and props
items.what: One job often has several names: head (7 families) beside header (13), action (7) beside actions (21), and trailing, end or header-action; description, lede or meta; media, preview or picture. Status holds four ideas, side mixes right and left with end and start, open, expanded and collapsed all mean show or hide, name is display text in 6 families and a form name in 5, one attribute uses British spelling, and the file called AppShell holds no app shell.
items.change: One name per job: header and footer, title, label, description (meta only for tabular facts), actions (action for a single built-in one), trailing, media and icon; status for outcomes only; logical side words; open for show and hide; name for the form name only; US spelling. Names migrate when a family is reopened, with aliases, a lint rejects new names outside the list, and the misnamed files are renamed with their own specs.
items.why: One vocabulary makes the API predictable across 125 families. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Saved themes need a migration for the renamed colours attribute.

items.title: Source files match families
items.what: Style files are not named by family: one holds Select, Table and Tabs, another seven families, and the surface file 10 blocks in 2,007 lines, while one React file has about 60 exports in 2,899 lines. Asset card carries 7 axes (4,320 combinations) while it is being retired into Design card, and Hatnote, Abbreviation and Timestamp are text styles of under 25 lines.
items.change: Files split to one style file and one React file per family, with no API or visual change. Asset card's axes retire into Design card as the shared frame lands, and the three text styles fold into a Text component only if that component is built.
items.why: Source that matches families can be changed one family at a time. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: It conflicts with every open branch, so it lands as one change when nothing else is open.

items.title: Release readiness and library defaults
items.what: The react, styles, tokens and output packages are at version 0.0.0 with no licence or changelog, Area's check does not run in CI, Calendar and Split button ignore the system's library defaults, and there is no export in the W3C design-token format.
items.change: Each package gets a version, a licence and a changelog, the check runs in CI, Calendar and Split button read the library defaults, and the output package can write the W3C design-token format.
items.why: Packages that leave the repository need a version, a licence and a CI check, and every family reads the library defaults. Confirmed in source; not needed before a release.
items.risk: The licence is the owner's choice.

items.title: Gaps take whole steps; only insets keep the half step
items.what: At type 13 the half density step is 0.5, and gaps are computed from it, so they land between rungs: the row gap is 10 px, Card's section gaps 14 and 18 px, Tabs 18 and 14 px, Stack's section 20 px, Choice rows 14 px, Description list's row gap 2 px and Card's carousel 7 px. Card's 11 px media corner and Tooltip's 9 px side come from the same half step.
items.change: Gaps read whole density steps, so each lands on its rung at Default: Card sections 16 and 20 px, Tabs 20 and 16 px, Stack's section 24 px, the palette footer and Choice rows 16 px, Description list rows 4 px apart, Card's carousel and well 8 px. Compact, the app's density, does not move, and the row gap waits for the menu density decision.
items.why: A gap reads whole steps and only an inset (edge to content) keeps the half step, as the theming guide already says. Confirmed in source and seen in the render.
items.risk: Default gets 2 px roomier in about a dozen gaps, against the references' direction for rows, which is why row gaps wait for the menu decision; the owner looks at Card and Tabs at Default.

items.title: Three roles for gaps between siblings
items.what: Gaps between siblings use four values with no stated roles, and Page header's actions, Drawer's stacked footer and the toast list are a fixed 8 px.
items.change: Those three follow the independent-controls gap (6, 8 or 10 px at density 28, 32 and 36), and the three roles are written down: a joined set 2 px, actions in a header or a line of text 4 px, independent controls 6 to 10 px.
items.why: Every gap between siblings belongs to one of three roles. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Nothing moves at Default.

items.title: Children spaced by their container's gap, not by margins
items.what: Eight places space children with a margin that subtracts the parent's gap, among them Card's title join, Card's carousel, Menu's shortcut column, Nav's groups (12 px), Shortcut list (32 px), Description list's “more”, Combobox's description and check, and Select's options.
items.change: Each pair that joins becomes its own group with its own gap, as Dialog's heading already does. Nothing visible changes at any setting.
items.why: A container spaces its children by its gap, and margins that undo it break under other settings. Confirmed in source; medium confidence that each case is clean to rebuild.
items.risk: A mis-set group gap would show as a regression, which the rendered check catches.

items.title: Name the section and page spaces
items.what: Stack's source says Area has no section token and doubles the row gap instead, and the feed kit's 32 and 48 px spaces are literals.
items.change: Two named roles, a section gap (24 px, Compact 16 px) and a page inset, are derived like the row gap, and Stack, the feed kit and Page header read them. No value changes.
items.why: A space used in several places becomes a named role; the published systems read name theirs.
items.risk: It adds token names, so it goes through the governance check for a role that names an existing value.

items.title: Two rhythms for text lists
items.what: Reference list rows sit 18 px apart with no gap, Link groups 22 px, Description list 26 px, and Accordion's plain items 2 px apart.
items.change: Reference list moves to 22 px and Accordion's items gain 6 px; Link groups and Description list stay as they are.
items.why: A text list (links, references, footnotes) is its line plus 4 px, a key-value list its line plus 8 px, and rows that are controls use the row ladder. Seen in the render.
items.risk: Reference list reads looser; the owner looks.

items.title: The Corner number is the medium control's real corner
items.what: The corner step is computed for a 32 px box, which was the medium control at type 14; at type 13 a medium Button draws 8 px while the step is 10. So Menu, Context menu, Command palette and List box rows are 10 px round (lists 14 px) while Nav and Tree rows of the same 30 px height, Buttons and field lists are 8 px.
items.change: The step becomes the medium control's corner at the current type and density, so floating-list rows move from 10 to 8 px and lists from 14 to 12 px at Corner 10, matching field lists; Kbd and Stepper follow, and the setting's description says “the corner of a medium control”.
items.why: Every full-width row takes its height's corner and the list around it follows concentrically. Confirmed in source and the render; live products' menu rows are 4–6 px.
items.risk: Menus become 2 px less round. This keeps the owner's Corner 10; making Corner 8 the default is an option in the corner decision.

items.title: Components read only public corner roles
items.what: File upload reads a raw setting value, Accordion's trigger, Step rows and Description list's “more” put 30 px rows on the 6 px small corner, Kbd rounds to 1 px, Stepper and Time field use private steps, and Table's frame is 14 px by its own formula beside Description list and Queue at 16 px and Plan's steps at 14 px.
items.change: A lint holds components to the public corner roles: full-width rows move from 6 to 8 px, Table's frame and Plan's steps join the shared block corner (14 to 16 px), File upload reads the container corner, and Kbd rounds down to 2 px or its documented sentence is corrected.
items.why: Components read named corner roles, never a literal or a private step, and blocks share one corner. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: A few rows and frames move by 2 px.

items.title: The corner default and how far surfaces step above controls
items.what: At Corner 10, controls round to 0.26–0.31 of their height, where live products sit at 0.125–0.25 (median 0.19). Card is 18 px over an 18 px inset, a corner equal to its padding where products use 0.375–0.58 of it, so a resting Card is rounder than the 16 px Popover that opens over it; Dialog is 20 px (container + 4), Asset card 20 px and Design card 24 px.
items.change: The owner chooses how far surfaces step above controls and whether Corner 10 stays the default. In every option, the two values furthest out of range are Card's 18 px and Dialog's extra 4 px.
items.why: A resting card is never rounder than the floating surface over it, and no product measured does otherwise. The desktop apps measured round surfaces 10–20 px over 5–8 px rows, and live products' cards are 6–14 px.

options.label: Keep Corner 10 and cap resting cards at the floating corner
options.detail: A Card's corner becomes 0.6 of its inset rounded down to an even pixel (10 px medium, 8 small, 12 large), Design and Asset card stop at 16 px, and Dialog drops its extra 4 px to 16 px while Popover and Panel keep 16. The owner's setting stays and the two outliers are fixed.

options.label: Keep Corner 10; every surface is the control corner + 4
options.detail: Surfaces, dialogs and cards become 12 px and rows 8 px, in the middle of the desktop apps measured (10–12 px). Every overlay loses 4 to 8 px of rounding.

options.label: Make Corner 8 the default
options.detail: Every control becomes 2 px less round (a medium control 6 px on 30 px, 0.2 of its height, the live products' median). It reverses the default set on 2026-10-26.

options.label: Keep everything
options.detail: Area stays rounder than every reference measured, and only the stale comments are fixed.

items.title: Dark muted text steps back as far as it does in light
items.what: Dark muted text is held at about #c5c5c5, so it is only 1.49:1 from the default #eeeeee and barely reads as a second level. Light is in range: muted #666666 is 5.74:1, and its step from the default (2.57) sits at the live products' median of 2.6, while dark live products step 2.2–3.1.
items.change: Dark muted moves to about #a0a0a0–#a6a6a6 (7.6–8.3:1 on black, about 4.7:1 on raised fills), and a test holds the step between default and muted. The 4.5:1 tests stay as they are.
items.why: Default and muted text keep the same step (2.0–3.2) in both themes, and muted stays at least 4.5:1 on the darkest fill it sits on. Seen in the render and in the live products; medium confidence on the exact value.
families: Every muted text and icon in dark
items.risk: Every dark screen changes, and muted text on raised fills must still pass 4.5:1, which the test enforces; the owner judges it on near-black.

items.title: A third text ink, and secondary and tertiary stop meaning the accent
items.what: Area has two text inks, default (138 rules) and muted (210), plus disabled (23) and a quiet ink for icon actions (3). Placeholder equals muted, the names secondary and tertiary point at the accent though every reference uses them for quieter text, and disabled is a fixed #a4a4a4 outside the layer model. Muted at 5.74:1 leaves little room above 4.5:1.
items.change: The owner decides whether meta that sits quieter than a description (shortcuts, timestamps, empty values, placeholders, line numbers) gets its own ink. In every option, the accent names are renamed and disabled is derived from the layer model.
items.why: The desktop apps measured use three or four text inks; the published systems split between two plus disabled and three.

options.label: Add a subtle ink at 4.5:1
options.detail: About #767676 on white, for placeholders, shortcuts, timestamps, empty values and line numbers, never for a description. A narrow step, but it meets the contrast floor for text.

options.label: Add a 3:1 ink for meta
options.detail: The quieter ink two desktop apps use, but it fails the WCAG AA text minimum, so only for non-essential meta. It conflicts with the rule never to weaken contrast.

options.label: Keep two inks
options.detail: As most published systems do; meta steps down by size (text-sm) instead.

items.title: Placeholders and unselected options each read one ink
items.what: Approval and Editable text paint placeholders in the muted ink instead of the placeholder role (the same colour today, but they would split if a theme changes it). Toggle group's outline and ghost off icons and Pagination's Previous and Next render at lightness 0.452, while Segmented, soft Toggle group, plate Tabs and Pagination's pages render 0.510.
items.change: The two placeholders read the placeholder role, Toggle group's outline and ghost off ink moves from 0.452 to 0.510, and Pagination's pages and Previous and Next share one ink.
items.why: Placeholders read one role, and every unselected option or inactive item in a bar reads muted. Confirmed in source and the render.
items.risk: The 0.452 ink may be a deliberate ghost-button step, so it stays on Button.

items.title: Tone colours the mark, never the words
items.what: Turn notice, Message, Attachment and File upload colour their status icons with the text ink, a deeper red than Toast's mark. Alert's title and link take the tone ink where Toast's stay default (an info title renders at lightness 0.506 against 0.277), and Tabs' change words paint an unselected label as loud as the selected one.
items.change: The four icons move one step brighter in light, a toned Alert's title and link turn default, and Tabs show status on a mark while the label keeps its selection ink.
items.why: Tone colours glyphs and marks, and a title or tab label keeps its own ink. Confirmed in source and the render.
items.risk: Toned Alerts read calmer, which matches the stated rule.

items.title: Dark hover and selected washes
items.what: In dark, hover paints 14% white, selected 19% and pressed 20.7%, so on the near-black page a hover plate lands near #262626. Light agrees with every reference at 5%. The desktop apps measured use 5–8% for hover and 10–15% for selected in dark.
items.change: The owner picks the dark hover and selected wash; it is solved so its contrast against the ground matches the light wash's. With the recommended values, hover becomes 8% and selected 14%, the press room and the 22% cap stay, and the muted-on-plate tests are rerun, not weakened.
items.why: Area's dark washes are two to three times every reference measured. Medium confidence: read from the products' declared values.

options.label: 8% hover / 14% selected
options.detail: Within half a point of the two closest desktop apps. The order of hover, selected and pressed is still guaranteed.

options.label: 5% hover / 10% selected
options.detail: The lightest reference's values. On near-black, plates behind muted rows may disappear.

options.label: Keep 14% / 19%
options.detail: Two to three times every reference.

items.title: Overlay motion: durations and an exit curve
items.what: Menus and popovers enter in 210 ms and leave in 140 ms, both easing out; tooltips take 140 ms, dialogs 280 ms in and 210 ms out, toasts 350 ms. The desktop apps measured animate menus in 0–150 ms and leave in about 100 ms, and the component libraries read use 150–200 ms.
items.change: Every anchored surface and dialog leaves on an exit curve that accelerates, whatever the duration. The owner picks the default durations.
items.why: Exits accelerate and never ease out into invisibility, and Area's menus are about twice as slow as the references. Strong evidence from every source read.

options.label: Anchored overlays fast both ways; dialogs on base
options.detail: Menus and popovers take 140 ms in and 140 ms out at Motion 210, close to the desktop apps, with no other duration moving.

options.label: Change the Motion default from 210 to 150
options.detail: Fast becomes 100 ms and base 150 ms, the products' numbers, but every transition in the system shortens.

options.label: Keep 210 and add only the exit curve
options.detail: The smallest change.

items.title: Surfaces opened by keyboard or used often appear at once
items.what: A menu opened by keyboard still plays the 210 ms scale, and the command palette shares Dialog's 280 ms in and 210 ms out. The motion guide asks for “the same short clock” but nothing provides it.
items.change: Overlays record whether the keyboard opened them; a keyboard or shortcut open, a context menu and the command palette skip the scale and only fade quickly. The palette takes the anchored overlays' durations, and opens at once from its shortcut.
items.why: The more often a surface opens, and the more directly, the shorter its animation; every source read agrees.
items.risk: Opens by pointer do not change.

items.title: A highlight moving through a list lands and leaves at once
items.what: Menu rows fade their plate in on hover (about 91 ms) and out in 140 ms, against the file's own comment that the plate lands at once, so a ghost plate trails one or two rows behind the pointer.
items.change: Row plates have no transition in Menu, List box, Custom select, Combobox, Command palette, Nav and Tree view. Standalone controls keep their eased hover.
items.why: A list highlight lands and leaves at once, as the platforms and libraries read do and Area's own rule says. One reference grows its plate instead; that was judged against.

items.title: Colour never overshoots; Spring becomes a real spring
items.what: One shared transition runs colour, border, shadow and scale on the same ease-out curve. Under Spring that curve overshoots, so a hover colour passes its target and comes back.
items.change: Colour, shadow and every fade read their own curve that never overshoots, and only movement reads Spring. Spring and the drawer curve become a true spring (damping 0.9, stiffness 700) drawn with linear() stops.
items.why: Only movement may overshoot, never colour or opacity. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Nothing changes at the default Subtle motion.

items.title: Hover colour on a shorter clock
items.what: Hover colour fades out on the fast duration, two thirds of Motion (140 ms at 210). Shipped products fade hover in 60–100 ms.
items.change: A new duration role at one third of Motion (70 ms at 210) drives colour changes; surfaces keep base.
items.why: A state change in colour should feel immediate. Medium confidence: from the products' and systems' declared values.
items.risk: Hover-off becomes crisper; the owner feels it in the app.

items.title: Press moves the plate, not the label
items.what: Pressing a button scales the whole control to 0.97 (0.96 small) in 91 ms, label included. Desktop apps measured scale either the whole control (0.98) or only the painted layer (0.975, released on a spring), and one also dims a pressed solid's label.
items.change: The owner decides how press feels. With the recommended option, the existing wash layer scales to 0.98, the label never moves or changes ink, and the release runs on the new spring.
items.why: A label that scales is resampled and blurs at 2×. Medium confidence: from declared values.

options.label: Press the plate, keep the label still
options.detail: The label never blurs at 2×; it feels like the closest desktop app.

options.label: Keep the whole-control press
options.detail: Today's behaviour, also used by one desktop app.

options.label: Also dim a pressed solid's label
options.detail: A cue without scale that still works with Feedback off; a matter of taste.

items.title: Progress fill animates by scale, not width
items.what: Progress and Meter animate their fill's width, which lays out the page on every frame.
items.change: The fill spans the full width and scales from its start edge.
items.why: Only transform and opacity animate, besides the documented size moves. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Between updates the fill sits at a fractional scale, which is fine for a bar.

items.title: A focus ring never sits flush on a fill of its own colour
items.what: The default Hug ring is 2 px with no offset, in the same neutral as the solid button fill at the defaults, so a focused solid Button looks 2 px larger rather than ringed.
items.change: Solid fills that match the ring take a 2 px gap or a 1 px inner line in the page colour, at every Focus ring setting. Other controls do not change.
items.why: Focus must read as a ring, never as a bigger button; every reference separates the two with a gap, an inner line or a second stroke. Not yet seen rendered.
items.risk: The owner looks at a focused solid Button in light and dark.

items.title: The focus placement table becomes a test
items.what: Accordion's trigger, Step rows and Token rows draw their row ring outside; Approval options and Prompt suggestions draw both a plate and a ring; Tag picker's ring has no offset; Time field's segments have none; Editable text draws a literal 1 px outline; and Composer's halo uses the shadow colour.
items.change: Each one is corrected, a test reads every focus rule against the table, and a ghost or plain control's ring drawn inside its own edge becomes a row of the table.
items.why: Controls ring outside with an offset, containers and text outside with a gap, and rows, tabs and cells inside, with one indicator per row. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Nothing changes at rest.

items.title: The focus ring answers Contrast More
items.what: Contrast More strengthens strokes and field outlines, but the focus ring stays as it is.
items.change: Under Contrast More the ring takes the gap and the 3 px Bold width, as one rule.
items.why: A higher-contrast setting should strengthen focus too, as the published systems read do.
items.risk: Nothing changes at Standard contrast.

items.title: Forced colours cover every state shown only by fill
items.what: Custom select, Date picker and Tag picker triggers and OTP slots lose their focus colour in forced colours, and soft Toggle group, Approval, List box grid, Custom select's grid preview and Design card show selection only by a fill or shadow, which forced colours removes.
items.change: Each gets a forced-colours rule, and a test reads every selector whose state is fill-only.
items.why: A state shown only by a fill or shadow vanishes in forced colours, so each needs its own rule. Read from source; not run in a forced-colours mode.
items.risk: Untested in a real forced-colours mode.

items.title: One edge per floating surface in dark
items.what: Every dark floating surface draws a 1 px 12.5% white border and a 16% rim outside it, a two-tone 2 px edge. Confirm dialog and Popover read as wireframes.
items.change: The dark floating edge becomes one 1 px line at about 16%. A brighter top line or a finer device-pixel ring could follow later, but that also needs floating lists to stop counting the border.
items.why: A surface draws one edge per side; every desktop app measured draws a single line in dark. Seen in the render and confirmed in source.
items.risk: Which line survives is a design call; the recommendation keeps the brighter rim's value as the one border.

items.title: Dark elevation and region depth
items.what: In dark, menus, dialogs and toasts paint the same tone as a Card (the menu samples rgb 2 on a page of rgb 1), separated only by the edge and a doubled shadow. With Layers at 0 on near-black there is no room for a lighter sidebar. In light, Area's menu shadow is lighter and shorter than the desktop apps' (about 12%).
items.change: The owner decides whether dark lifts each elevation one layer step (page, cards, floating, modal) and whether the chrome ground gets a dark floor. The page stays near black in every option, and the light half waits for the Layers 50 merge.
items.why: The published systems read all lighten raised surfaces in dark instead of relying on shadow alone.

options.label: Dark lifts floating and modal surfaces one layer step
options.detail: A menu over a card becomes about #1a1a1a over #121212, and light does not change. With the single dark edge, this is the separation every reference uses.

options.label: Also give the chrome ground a dark floor
options.detail: The sidebar sits 2–3 lightness points above the page. It changes chat, document, code editor and design tool layouts.

options.label: Keep one sheet and separate by rules
options.detail: Today's look, relying on the single dark edge.

options.label: Revisit the light floating shadow
options.detail: A 12% near layer, as both closest desktop apps use; Floating 8 stays the setting.

items.title: The control height ladder at type 13
items.what: At type 13 Default, controls are 22, 26, 30, 38 and 46 px with 30 px rows; the app's Compact gives 20, 24, 26, 34 and 42 px with 28 px rows. The desktop apps measured use 24 px at 13 px text (one 32 px), the published systems 24, 32, 40 and 48 px, and live products 32 px at 14 px text, a 2.29 ratio to text that Area's 30 px at 13 matches (2.31). Some parts are written on the 4 px ladder and sit off Area's.
items.change: The owner picks the default heights. In every option heights stay derived from the line, so text stays exactly centred, and parts written for the 4 px ladder read Area's ladder tokens.
items.why: By the ratio of height to text Area is inside the live products' range; the desktop apps are denser and the web systems taller, so the references pull in opposite directions.

options.label: Keep the derived ladder and the Default density
options.detail: By ratio to text Area sits inside every live product, and the app already runs Compact (medium 26 px, 2 px from the desktop apps). Snapping to 4 px would either merge small and medium at Compact or move the app's medium to 28 px, away from the desktop apps.

options.label: Make density 28 the default for type 13 and below
options.detail: Compact ships as the default (medium 26 px, rows 28 px), so library users get desktop density.

options.label: Snap heights to a 4 px ladder
options.detail: Type 13 Default becomes 24, 28, 32, 40 and 48 px and the app 20, 24, 28, 36 and 44 px. Medium Buttons grow 2 px.

options.label: Allow a 22 px row floor for dense tools
options.detail: Below the 24 px target minimum (WCAG 2.5.8) unless the shared hit target carries it.

items.title: Rows and composite parts on the height ladder
items.what: Eight row heights between 21 and 56 px come from literals: Calendar days 28, 30 or 34 px (28 px beside a 24 px control at type 12 Compact), Description list rows +2 px, Shortcut list rows +4 px, Plan's head +8 px, Prompt suggestions 42–48 px, Board's add row 34 px, Asset row 56 px and Token row 21 px.
items.change: Heights read a ladder token plus whole room steps: Calendar days become the medium control and cells that plus 4 px (2 px shorter at Compact), Description list rows the row height (2 px shorter), Shortcut list a row plus one stack step, Board's add row a row (4–6 px shorter), and Token row a mark or small control height.
items.why: A height is a ladder token or a ladder token plus whole steps, never a literal 2 or 4 px. Medium confidence, since each literal came from one measured product.
items.risk: Each literal came from one measured product, so the owner confirms each family.

items.title: Heading hierarchy: components adopt the heading weight and title-xl
items.what: On this branch nothing goes above 20/28 for words or above 500 for weight; the merge brings a 600 heading weight and a 32/40 title-xl that no component reads yet. Page header small (16/22 500) equals Section heading, medium is 18/24 and large 20/28. The live products measured title pages at 20–40 px and weights 590–700.
items.change: After the merge, Page header medium is 24/32 at the heading weight and large is title-xl, Section heading stays 16/500, so page, section and card titles read 24, 16 and 13. Titles from title-sm up take the heading weight, and Message gains two heading levels.
items.why: A screen shows three levels (page, section, item) told apart by size and weight. Every rendered product does it; Area stops at 500.
items.risk: The title-balance pass of 2026-11-06 set sizes and gaps, not this weight, so the owner confirms which titles take 600.

items.title: The smallest text size is for marks only
items.what: Many words are set at 11/14: Field's error and count, Slider's ends, Calendar's days, Asset row, small Panel labels, Select's group labels, Color picker's heading, Composer menu's path (13 in Command palette), the palette's footer hints and Menu's shortcuts, many with comments saying 12/16. Field's count sits about 1 px off its description's baseline, and Calendar's numerals are 11 px in 30 px cells.
items.change: Each moves to 12/16, Composer menu's path to 13, Asset row's name to 13/18 over 12/16 meta, and Calendar's days to 12 or 13 (the owner picks; both fit 30 px cells). A test lists the parts allowed the smallest size.
items.why: The 11/14 size is only for Badge, Count, Kbd, Indicator, Citation, data labels and status letters; words that label, explain, warn or locate are at least 12. Confirmed in source and the render.
items.risk: Rows with these labels grow 2 px per line.

items.title: One rule for joined lines and one for title pairs
items.what: A line joined to a name is 12 px muted in eleven families (Choice, Switch, Menu, Field, Meter, File tile, Hover card, Section heading's lede and others) and 13 px muted in eight more (Setting row, Approval, Stepper, Board, Timeline and every surface description). So a Switch is 13 over 12 and the same setting in a Setting row is 13 over 13. Title to description is 4 px (owner, 2026-11-06); products use 2–8 px.
items.change: The owner picks the direction, and the rule is written once in the design system and the type skill.
items.why: A step changes one property at a time, and the same pair reads the same way everywhere. Medium confidence: the references differ on both questions.

options.label: A joined line is the name's size, in muted ink
options.detail: Smaller text is kept for text set apart from what it explains. Choice, Switch, group descriptions, Custom select, File tile, Hover card and Section heading's lede move from 12 to 13 (rows grow 2 px per line); Field, Meter and small Empty state stay 12, and Menu's 12 is kept as the dense-menu exception. Surface titles keep their weight and ink step, and Confirm dialog's default-ink description is the written exception.

options.label: A joined line steps down to text-sm everywhere
options.detail: Setting row, Approval, Stepper and surface descriptions move from 13 to 12. Denser, but two properties change at once.

options.label: Also widen the title pair gap from 4 to 8 px
options.detail: On Card, Dialog, Empty state and Page header, with compact surfaces keeping 4. It is independent of the choice above, reverses the 2026-11-06 pick, and rests on three sources.

items.title: One treatment for a heading over a run of rows
items.what: Menu, Nav, List box, Combobox, the palette and Shortcut list label a run of rows at the rows' size, 500, muted. Panel's heading, Link groups, Reference list and Table of contents use 500 in the default ink; Select's group label and Color picker's heading are 11/400 muted; Table's group heading is 400 default; and the type skill still calls 500 muted a mistake.
items.change: Select's group label and Color picker's heading become 13/500 muted, and the skill is rewritten to match. Whether Panel's heading, Link groups, Reference list and Table of contents turn muted is the owner's confirmation.
items.why: A label over a run of rows is the rows' size, 500, muted and a row tall (owner, 2026-10-22); a title that names a whole surface stays in the default ink.
items.risk: Panel's heading ink is the owner's pick; one design tool measured uses a firmer default-ink heading.

items.title: One table of weights
items.what: The docs disagree with the code on weights: one line says strong is only for labels on fills, another that larger titles are 400 (all are 500), another that soft Count is 500 (it is 400). Item names are 500 in File tile, File upload, Asset row and Board card and 400 in nine other families.
items.change: One weight table, quoted by the type skill and the typography source, and item names moved to one weight.
items.why: 500 is for titles of a surface or region, group labels, labels on fills and marks and the selected tab; 400 for everything read or operated, figures included. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: It follows the decision on item names.

items.title: A regular weight above 400, and lighter weights in dark
items.what: Regular text is 400 and strong 500. Several shipped products set regular at 430–510 and strong at 550–590, and one lowers every weight by 40 in dark; Area's typeface is variable and its weight ramp already holds 450.
items.change: The owner chooses the Typography setting's default regular weight, and whether dark lowers weights to offset glow on black. Every option keeps the setting's existing values.
items.why: Light text on black reads heavier than the same weight on white; a slightly firmer regular is common in the products measured. Medium confidence: declared values only.

options.label: Try 430–450 as the default regular
options.detail: Body text, menus and fields become a touch firmer, and the gap from regular to strong narrows from 100 to about 60. To look at before deciding.

options.label: Lower weights by 40 in dark
options.detail: Dark text reads the same weight as light text, on near-black.

options.label: Keep 400 / 500
options.detail: As several published systems and one desktop app do.

items.title: Label weight on quiet buttons
items.what: Every Button variant labels at 500 (the owner's pick on 2026-10-08). The desktop apps measured use 400 on quiet variants and 500 on primary; the live web products' median is 500 on all.
items.change: If changed, solid buttons keep 500 and quiet variants take 400, as one rule.
items.why: The live web products agree with Area, and one weight avoids changes between neighbouring buttons.

options.label: Keep 500
options.detail: The live web products agree with Area, and neighbouring buttons never change weight.

options.label: 400 on soft, outline and ghost
options.detail: The desktop apps' choice: toolbars and dialog footers lose weight and the primary stands out.

items.title: Tabular figures wherever numbers change or align
items.what: Number field (whose width jitters while scrubbing), Timestamp, Nav's trailing counts, Date picker's value, Slider's ends and ordinary Table cells use proportional figures; Tree view and Menu already use tabular ones.
items.change: Each sets tabular figures, and a test reads a list of numeric parts.
items.why: A number that updates, counts or sits in a column uses tabular figures so it does not shift. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Fixed type sizes in Kbd, code and the smallest labels
items.what: Small Kbd and every Kbd in a menu are a fixed 11 px on a 10 px line, small beside 13 px text. Code block small and Diff use a 17 px line, the system's only odd line, and ignore Type; inline Code renders 11.375/15.36 in a 21.38 px box taller than its line. Folder and File page labels compute to 6, 8 or 12 px, and Citation's footnote is 9.15 px.
items.change: Kbd reads the smallest text size at every size (no change at 13, larger at 14–16), Code block small and Diff move from 11/17 to 11/16, inline Code inherits its line (box at most 18 px), and folder and file labels and the footnote stay at 10 px or more, or are hidden as artwork.
items.why: Mark and code text follow the Type setting, code leading is a role on it, and no text goes under 10 px. Confirmed in source and the render.
items.risk: Whether folder labels are text or artwork has to be checked in the React source.

items.title: Tracking and underline offset as tokens
items.what: Small text's tracking is applied by 9 rules out of hundreds (0.03–0.08 px, invisible), the donut chart's centre misses its title tracking, 0.08 em is written in seven places, Badge plain uses 0.2 em and Description list's “more” none. The products measured disagree on small-text tracking because their typefaces differ.
items.change: Text below 14 px gets no tracking (as Badge already does), larger sizes keep their token's, and one underline-offset token is read everywhere. Weight-dependent small tracking waits for an on-screen check.
items.why: Tracking belongs to the type token, and a single underline offset keeps links consistent. Medium confidence: the references point in different directions.
items.risk: Nothing visible changes below 14 px.

items.title: One role for figures
items.what: Card's value and Chart's figure are 26/400 sans with tabular figures, but the donut's centre is 18/500 monospace without its title tracking, and chart ticks and notes are monospace 11 beside a sans legend.
items.change: The owner decides chart text; then figures are sans, 400, tabular, at title-lg or title-sm with their tracking, and monospace stays only where characters align by column. With the recommended option, the donut's centre is sans 400 and ticks are sans, tabular and muted.
items.why: Dashboards in the reference set use the interface's sans with tabular figures.

options.label: Sans tabular ticks and centre
options.detail: Dashboards in the reference set use the interface's sans with tabular figures.

options.label: Keep monospace data labels
options.detail: The spec's deliberate choice.

items.title: Reading size only where prose is written
items.what: Prompt suggestions, Command palette's step and input, and Accordion's medium trigger are 15/22 (Accordion's comment claims 16/24).
items.change: The palette's step moves to 13 while its input stays 15 (the owner's pick), and Accordion is handled with the content round.
items.why: A field you write prose into, and options that become that prose, take the reading size; every other operated part takes the base size.
items.risk: A small change.

items.title: A label beside a value is muted 400; the value leads
items.what: Description list's terms are 500 default when justified or framed, Filter bar's “Label: Value” is one run in one ink, Progress labels at 400 with the value default while Meter labels at 500 with the value muted, and their gaps are 8 and 6 px.
items.change: Description list terms are muted 400 in every layout, Filter bar's label muted and value default, and Progress and Meter both label 13/400 default with the value 13/400 muted and tabular, 6 px above the bar.
items.why: Layout moves a label, never its role, so a label beside its value is muted and the value leads. Seen in the render and confirmed in source.
items.risk: Justified Description list loses its title look.

items.title: Light plates and wells: measure again after the merge
items.what: Content plates sit only 1.04:1 off the light ground but 0.115 lighter in dark, so the user's message bubble, Empty state's plate, the neutral Alert, Attachment, Approval options, inline Code, Citation and Card's media plates nearly vanish in light and read as solid blocks in dark. Shipped chat bubbles sit near #f4f4f4.
items.change: Plates that carry content get a step of about #f2f2f2 in light and about #1a1a1a on #0b0b0b in dark, preferably as a new plate role. The light half waits for the new Layers 50 ground to be measured first.
items.why: A plate or well sits the same perceived step off its ground in light and dark. Low confidence for light, because it was measured at Layers 0.
items.risk: The light values were measured before the light default moved to 50, so nothing light changes until they are measured again; the dark half stands.

items.title: Dark tone inks balanced in strength
items.what: In dark, danger's edge is much less saturated than success's (chroma 0.092 against 0.216; warning 0.110), so an invalid field reads pale pink beside a vivid green success. Light is the reverse (danger 0.234, success 0.148).
items.change: Dark tone inks are solved again to one saturation band per role, with danger at least as strong as success, as part of the colour work.
items.why: Tones of one role read with one strength, and danger never reads weaker than success. Measured in the render.
items.risk: The palette file is preserved and the contrast tests gate the change.

items.title: Empty boxes, rules and connectors keep their edge in dark
items.what: In dark, unchecked Checkbox and Radio edges are about 2.4:1 and empty field and OTP edges about 1.6:1; Separator, Badge borders, Count and Tag rings and the Step rail are 7.5%, Stepper's connectors vanish, and Plan's pending ring is 1.1:1 in a chat. In light, Alignment picker's well disappears on the gallery ground.
items.change: Boxes that are the whole control when empty take the hover edge in both themes, dividers and mark edges move from 7.5% to 10%, Stepper's connectors take the control stroke with completed segments in the default ink, and Plan's pending ring takes the control edge.
items.why: An empty box that is the whole affordance keeps a visible edge, and rules never drop below 10%. Seen in the render.
items.risk: It only strengthens edges; the exact step is chosen by eye.

items.title: Chart series reach 3:1 as lines in each theme
items.what: On white, the blue series is 2.85:1, pink 2.73:1 and yellow 1.83:1 (indigo 4.09:1); in dark every series is at least 4.8:1.
items.change: Each light series step deepens to at least 3:1 as a 1.5 px line; bars may stay lighter with a 1 px darker edge. The bright hue families stay.
items.why: A chart line must reach 3:1 against its ground (WCAG non-text contrast). Measured in the render.
items.risk: The owner wants bright colours, so only the light step moves.

items.title: Every derived inset lands on a whole pixel
items.what: Empty lines in Combobox, Tag picker, Composer menu and Command palette, native Select options and Card's heading beside a control compute their padding without rounding (10.38 px at Default). Table of contents text sits at 0.6 px, and Checkbox and Radio cards are 48.61 px tall.
items.change: Text moves by 0.38 px at every density, card heights round up to whole pixels, and a test rejects any cap-centred padding that skips the rounding.
items.why: Every derived inset is rounded to a whole pixel through the shared inset list. Confirmed in source and the render.

items.title: One shared hit target: 24 px by pointer, 44 px by touch
items.what: Eleven families have targets under 24 px with no hit expansion: Input actions and Number field steps (16–22 px), Chip's dismiss, Nav row actions (20–22 px), Split button's icon trigger (15 × 30 px), small Segmented and Toggle group items, Breadcrumb's ellipsis (16 px), small swatches and Step rows (18 px). Only five families grow their target for touch.
items.change: Any interactive box under 24 px carries a centred invisible target of at least 24 px, or 44 px under a coarse pointer, as one shared utility. Nothing visible changes; small Segmented items overlap their neighbours' targets by 1–2 px.
items.why: Every interactive box has a 24 px target (WCAG 2.5.8), 44 px for touch. Confirmed in source; target sizes at Compact were computed, not hit-tested.
items.risk: Targets can overlap in tight toolbars, which the behaviour tests check.

items.title: Glyphs at their native sizes
items.what: File upload's glyph is a fixed 20 px, Empty state's is computed from the icon cut, and File page scales its icon to 30 px at 96 px.
items.change: File page's icon moves from 30 to 32 or 24 px, and File upload reads an icon size token or records its size in the spec.
items.why: A glyph's box is one of the native sizes (10, 12, 16, 20, 24 px), and scaled figures snap to the nearest one. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Truncated single lines keep their descenders
items.what: Fifty truncating text rules pad nothing below the line, so descenders such as g, y and p may clip; this was not checked in the render.
items.change: The rendered check looks for clipping first. Only if it finds any, every truncating box pads its block by 0.125 em and takes it back with a negative margin.
items.why: A truncated line should never cut its letters. Low confidence: one desktop app does this, and Area's clipping is unverified.

items.title: One frame recipe and one frame prop
items.what: No family shares a frame: selected strokes are painted in 5 files, the frame is spelled five ways, and card-like frames render seven corners (14 px Table; 16 px Board, Panel, Video, Figure and framed Description list; 18 px Card and Surface; 19 px Composer; 20 px Asset card against a spec of 16; 21 px large Card; 24 px Design card). Surface uses a 14 px inset, a 10 px gap and a 16/22 title over a 12 px lede beside Card's 18, 14 and 13 over 13; a soft Surface pads 14 px while painting nothing, and nested wells fall to a 4 px corner.
items.change: Every card-like frame reads one recipe: the container corner from the corner decision, the inset ladder, the title pair, and nested corners that stop at the 8 px row corner by shrinking the wrapper's pad. One frame prop (surface, soft or plain) replaces the five spellings, content kind becomes its own prop, Surface and Card share inset, gap and title, and an unpainted region takes no inset.
items.why: Card-like frames are one part, so they share one corner, inset and title. Seen in the render across seven corners.
items.risk: The largest visible change in the plan: every card corner and Surface's inset move, and Asset card's retirement rides on it. The soft Surface case must be measured again at the new light default first.

items.title: One name part for picture cards
items.what: Picture cards place their name in five ways: above at 13.4 px and 400 (Asset card), below inside at 18 px and 500 (Card), and below outside at 4 px (Design card), 0 px (Figure) or centred (File tile), at 400 or 500. Two earlier card decisions already disagree on where names sit.
items.change: The owner picks the weight. Then every picture card uses one name part: one weight, 8 px from the picture outside a frame or the inset inside it, no indent outside an unframed picture, and position stays a prop with one geometry each; Design card's 4 px indent becomes 0.
items.why: An item name is one part with one look wherever it appears. Seen in the render.

options.label: 500 in the default ink for every item name
options.detail: Card, File tile and Board card already do this, and Asset and Design card gain weight. A caption stays 12 px muted.

options.label: 400 for names
options.detail: What one design-system sentence says; Card, File tile and Board card lose weight.

items.title: One chat card
items.what: Within a few rows a transcript shows three corners and three insets: Composer 19 px with a 16 px inset, Approval 19 px with 12 px, Plan, Queue and Edit summary 16 px with 13 px (Edit summary's head 34 px), Message 16 px with 14 px, Code block 13 px and 11.5 px with 11 and 15 px insets, Diff 4 px and Attachment 8 px with 11 px. The desktop apps measured each hold one corner.
items.change: Chat cards share the container corner, a 12 px text inset with the border counted once, a 30 px head and a 13/18 500 title. Plan, Queue and Edit summary text moves 1 px in, Code block's corners move from 13 and 11.5 to 16 px (or 10), and Edit summary's head from 34 to 30 px; Composer and Approval keep the composer corner with the same inset.
items.why: Cards in one column share one corner and one inset. Seen in the render.
items.risk: The corner value follows the corner decision.

items.title: The bottom of a text-only Card
items.what: A Card's title cap sits 18 px from the top, but the last line is trimmed to its descent, so its baseline sits about 22.6 px from the bottom edge and text-only cards look 4–5 px heavier at the bottom.
items.change: The owner decides whether the last line trims to its baseline plus a fixed allowance for descenders (about 16 px from baseline to edge) instead of its descent.
items.why: A text-only card should look even at top and bottom. Measured in the render; the current trim is a recorded rule.

options.label: Trim to the baseline plus an allowance
options.detail: Top and bottom look even. To look at before deciding.

options.label: Keep the descent trim
options.detail: The recorded rule.

items.title: One table of row values
items.what: Rows of the same height disagree: Menu, Command palette and List box rows are 10 px round while Nav and Tree rows are 8 px, text-only rows start 10 px or 8 px in, and row icons are the default ink in Menu, Nav and the palette but muted in Tree view, so the sidebar shows both. Nav's separator is a fixed 9 px where Menu's is 5–7 px, Nav's group break a fixed 12 px, Select's options 2 px apart by margin, separators inset 8 px while text starts at 13–14 px, and Nav's picture rows start labels at 38 px beside 34.
items.change: Rows share one table: their height's corner, one text-only edge, muted icons at rest in Menu and Nav, Nav's separator at 5–7 px with its ends on the plates' edges, Nav's group break at the row gap, Select's options 1 px apart, and picture lists reserving the picture's width on every row.
items.why: Rows are one part, so they share corner, edge, icon ink and separators. Every reference sets row icons a step lighter than the label.
items.risk: The direction of the icon ink is a pick.

items.title: One way to centre a single line of text
items.what: Button, Chip, Segmented, Menu, Nav, Command palette and List box centre their text exactly, but Custom select, Date picker, Time field, Number field units, Selection bar's count, Tabs, Tree view, Pagination, Panel row labels and Tooltip sit 0.6 px high. Switch's label is 0.61 px above its track on all 22 tiles while Checkbox and Radio are exact, and in one Input the affix and the value sit on different lines (“+1” and “1”).
items.change: Every one-line label or value in a control, row or tab uses the cap-trimmed span; native inputs are offset by the same amount (0.61 px at type 13), and a second text beside a trimmed one is trimmed too. A rendered check holds it.
items.why: Text in a control, row or tab is centred on its capitals. Measured on every tile.
items.risk: These are 0.6 px moves based on an inferred ascent, so the rendered check confirms the amount first.

items.title: Menu density and the label column
items.what: Menu rows are 30 px (28 at Compact) with a 10 px gap from icon to label (8 at Compact), so labels start at 34 px (32), and lists are at least 224 px wide with no cap. The desktop apps measured use 24 px rows, a 6 px gap, labels at 30 px and lists 120–128 px wide with a 320 px cap; live products' nav rows use 8 px. Making gaps whole steps alone would move this gap to 12 px, away from every reference.

items.title: One field shell

items.title: Two header bar heights

items.title: A corner control is concentric with its surface

The plates round to 11, 9, 5 and 6 px, Panel's action moves 7 px out, and Color picker's control 3 px in.

items.title: Edge ghost buttons put their glyph on the text column

Filled and outline controls keep their plate on the column.

items.risk: Card's note of 2026-09-28 chose the plate edge for vertical position only; Message's actions while streaming are handled in the conversation round.

items.title: One collapsible card head
items.what: Plan's title is 400 default with the chevron after it, Queue's 400 muted with the chevron at the far end, Edit summary's 400 default in a 34 px head, and Approval's 500.

items.title: One mark
items.what: Marks disagree: Badge is 18 px with 11 px text at 500 and 6 px sides, Count the same at 400, Tag 13 px text with 5 px sides and a 4 px corner, Kbd 11 px text on a 10 px line with 4 px sides (22 px tall in Approval, 14 px in its hint), Citation 7 px sides on a solid fill with text 0.6 px high, Indicator's count 16 px at 500, inline Code 21.38 px, and Mention 21 px in an 18 px line so wrapped chips overlap by 3 px. Tag's sides become 6 (8 large), Kbd's 6 with a 14 px line, Citation's 6 with its text lowered 0.6 px, Mention 18 px, and Badge Plain takes the mark weight; the identical inverse looks are made distinct or dropped.

At Compact the small and medium mark labels are both 14 px, so Badge, Count, Kbd and Tag look identical at the two sizes in the app.

items.title: One counter
items.what: Count is 18 px at 400, while Indicator's count is 16 px at 500 built from 16 px + 2 px literals, and the docs list Count as 16 / 20 px though it renders 14 / 18.
