items.title: One shadow stack for every floating surface
items.what: Calendar's and Color picker's surfaces and Select's picker draw only an edge and a float shadow and are missing from the Material setting's list, so under a glass material a glass Menu would sit beside an opaque date grid. items.title: A surface's gap between blocks never exceeds its inset

items.title: Write down the overlay corner table
items.what: Command palette is 14 px round beside Dialog and Confirm dialog at 20 px, though all three are modal. A medium Split button and a medium Custom select, both 30 px tall, open lists at 14 and 12 px; Number field's unit list is 10 px, Calendar's caption menu 12 px, and date and filter popovers 16 px. The palette's 600 px and Confirm dialog's 420 px widths are literals with no public width settings.

The palette's frame takes the modal corner with its list nested concentrically inside (or the table says why it counts as a list), and Dialog, Drawer and Command palette gain public width hooks.

items.risk: Whether the palette is a list or a modal is a design call.

items.title: One footer button pair and one dialog title group

Dialog's title shifts 2.8 px depending on whether a close button is present, and its description is untrimmed.

items.title: Alert and Toast agree

items.title: One look for a trigger whose popup is open

Custom select's ghost takes the selected plate, Date picker the focus edge (an open Combobox shows a 2 px ring while Custom select shows none), Toggletip the active plate, Breadcrumb's ellipsis the hover plate, and Nav's row actions nothing.

items.what: Nav, plate Tabs, List box's grid and Pagination show a press over the selected item, but Menu, Tree view, Table, Calendar, Approval and toggle Buttons do not.

items.why: Every hover plate has a pressed plate one step past it. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Literal fills become roles

Soft Toggle group presses to the selected wash while its twin uses a literal, Property list uses literal opacities, and Diff and Code block paint added and removed lines differently. Selected text on the inverse Tooltip goes near-black on near-black.

Justified literals (media chrome, gradients, Slider's grip and a few others) are marked as spec values.

Native Select shows the check alone in the text colour (Menu's check uses the selection colour), with an 11/400 group label and disabled options dimmed by ink; its spec chose the check alone.

Calendar days and Select options move to opacity, Property list reads the token, and Setting row's description stays muted with its label muted as in Field.

options.detail: A disabled danger action stops reading as an available one.

items.title: Read-only is visible and keeps the chosen state
items.what: On eight fields, read-only changes nothing but the pointer, a checked read-only choice card loses its selected edge, and Radio group spells the attribute differently from the rest.

items.title: One way to reveal on hover
items.what: Half the hover reveals hide their content and then restore it for touch with a separate rule (Attachment, Message, Nav and Panel chevrons, Queue, Prompt suggestions, Property list, Step, Card's overlay, Tree actions, Edit summary, Asset card); the other half hide only where hover exists.

items.title: An inactive row dims as a whole
items.what: Menu's inactive title is at 50% opacity (about lightness 0.64) while its note stays at full strength (0.510), so the reason line is darker than the title.

items.risk: It revisits a recorded reason while keeping the note legible.

items.title: Selection as a scope
items.what: Selected paint is written family by family, so each child of a selected row needs its own rule.

items.why: One design tool measured remaps its colours under a selected scope; it removes per-family rules. Medium confidence; not needed now.

items.title: Twin components share one recipe
items.what: Segmented and soft Toggle group look identical at the defaults but read different stroke and pill settings, so they part at Stroke 0 or 2. There are two tab strips (Tabs with plate, status and unseen marks; horizontal Nav with closes), and Checkbox and Radio come in medium and large while Switch comes in small, medium and large.

items.why: Twins share one recipe so a setting cannot pull them apart. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Nothing changes at the defaults.

items.title: Spacing that ignores density beside peers that follow it
items.what: About fifteen families use fixed spaces where their peers follow density: Asset row (8 and 12 px), Board's cards and header, Setting row's 16 px from text to control, Page header's actions, Stepper and Timeline (12 px), large Tabs (24 px), OTP slots (8 px), Alert's icon gap, Menu's two-line block, Empty state, Drawer's footer, the toast list, Table's caption and Shortcut list's groups (32 px).
items.change: Each reads its density role, moving 2 or 4 px at Compact and Comfortable and nothing at Default; Setting row's gap reads the medium surface inset, with a wider 20 px option noted for the owner.
items.why: Space between pieces of UI follows density unless it is a mark, a hit area, a platform constant or a measured media size. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Each was a spec decision, so the owner confirms each family at Compact and Comfortable.

items.title: One menu engine, with submenus that wait for the pointer
items.what: A submenu opens the moment the pointer enters its row and closes as soon as a sibling is focused, while the parent focuses every row the pointer crosses, so a diagonal move closes the submenu and brushing past a menu flashes every submenu. Five separate menu engines exist; only one syncs pointer and focus, so two rows can highlight at once, and there are three Tab behaviours and four item selectors (Split button skips checkbox and radio rows).
items.change: One shared menu navigation (keys, typeahead, pointer and focus in step, one rule for which choices close the menu) and one pointer-intent hook: a submenu opens after 100 ms of rest, or at once by click or key, and a safe triangle with a 5 px margin keeps the parent from stealing focus or closing for up to 300 ms. Hover card reuses the hook, and the motion guide gains a submenu row.
items.why: Reaching a submenu diagonally must not close it; the component libraries read wait 100–200 ms and use a safe area. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Behaviour can regress, so the browser tests come first.

items.title: Choosers act on press, and press-drag-release picks
items.what: Menus open on click, Custom select opens on click and Tabs select on click, one press slower than the platforms and libraries read, and none lets you press, drag to an item and release to pick it.
items.change: Menus, selects, tabs and segmented controls act on the pointer press (left button, no modifier) and support press-drag-release: armed after 200 ms or 5 px, ignoring a release within 10 px. Click stays for touch and keyboard.
items.why: Choosing from a menu or a strip should take one press. Strong evidence from the platforms and libraries read.
items.risk: The native popover opens on click, so double toggles must be guarded.

items.title: What a press outside an open menu does
items.what: With the native popover, the press that dismisses a menu also activates whatever lies under it. Desktop platforms and modal menus in the libraries read swallow that press.
items.change: The owner decides, and the choice is written in the overlay spec. To swallow, the first outside press while a menu is open is intercepted.
items.why: Dismissing a menu should never press a button by accident.

options.label: Swallow the press
options.detail: As desktop platforms do: dismissing never presses a button by accident.

options.label: Let it pass through
options.detail: The web default: one click does two things.

items.title: One list navigation and one typeahead
items.what: Six families draw their own list box, the down arrow is handled in 21 files and Home and End in 14, and typeahead is written five ways: Menu, List box and Tree wait 1000 ms, Custom select 500 ms and alone cycles on a repeated letter, Menu builds “aa” and finds nothing, and Tree assumes a text label.
items.change: One list navigation hook (active item, wrap, Home and End, Page Up and Down, skipping disabled items) and one grid navigation hook, plus one typeahead with one reset window, repeated-letter cycling, Space inside a run and a text fallback. They are tested once and adopted one family at a time.
items.why: Lists behave the same in every family, tested once. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: The largest behaviour change in the plan.

items.title: One model for moving focus with arrow keys
items.what: There are three focus models. Toolbar and Toggle group forward focus from the container, so Shift+Tab lands on the container and an empty toolbar is a Tab stop; Segmented and Toggle group take both arrow axes while Tabs and Toolbar take one; Tree's row actions are extra Tab stops.
items.change: One hook gives each composite (Toolbar, Toggle group, Segmented, Tabs, List box, Tree view) one Tab stop with arrows by orientation. A tree's row actions are reached with the right arrow, Accordion gains optional up, down, Home and End, and * expands a tree's siblings.
items.why: A composite control is one Tab stop, moved through with arrows, as WAI-ARIA describes. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Keyboard behaviour can regress, which the browser tests catch.

items.title: Key fixes in list families
items.what: Tag picker uses retired remove props and makes every tag a Tab stop, Combobox builds group ids from their label text so a label with a space leaves the group unnamed, and Command palette moves only with the arrows and Ctrl+Home and End.
items.change: Tags use the current dismiss props and are reached with the left arrow from the empty field (Backspace or Delete removes), group ids come from their position, and the palette also takes Ctrl+N and P and Ctrl+J and K.
items.why: Each is a defect against the list rules. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Required, reset, name and value in every form control
items.what: Hidden inputs cannot be required, so Custom select marks only its accessible state, and Combobox, Date picker, Date range picker, Tag picker, Time field, Segmented and Toggle group have no required at all: forms submit empty. Fourteen files copy one reset block, and seven families ignore a form reset.
items.change: Every value family renders one hidden native control that carries name, required and custom validity, focuses the visible control when invalid and listens for reset, from one shared hook, and a test checks reset and required on every family with a name.
items.why: A form control must take part in its form. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Native validation bubbles appear where there were none.

items.title: Typing guards for text entry
items.what: While someone confirms a candidate in an input method (for Chinese, Japanese or Korean), Enter in Command palette runs the highlighted command, Approval's “instead” field submits, and Color field commits; Date picker, Editable text and Zoom control miss the same case. Pressing Shift halfway through a Number field scrub multiplies the whole distance.
items.change: Every Enter handler on a text input calls one helper that ignores composition, held by a test, and Number field's scrub restarts from the current value when a modifier changes.
items.why: Enter during composition confirms the text, never the form. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Nothing changes for typing without an input method.

items.title: Toasts above every modal, paused when unseen
items.what: The toast region is a plain section with a z-index while every modal and popover sits in the top layer, so a toast raised during a dialog renders under the backdrop and cannot be used (Undo cannot be pressed, the F8 key cannot reach it). Timers pause only on hover and focus, so toasts expire while the window is in the background.
items.change: The toast region becomes a manual popover, shown again whenever a toast is added so it is the newest top-layer entry, and moves into an open modal as the announcer does. Timers pause when the window is hidden or loses focus and resume with the time left.
items.why: A toast must be usable whatever is open. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: The order among nested popovers in the top layer is checked by the browser tests.

items.title: Arrows point at their trigger, and surfaces leave with it
items.what: Arrows sit at the middle of every side, so start-aligned popovers, Hover card's default and surfaces shifted at the viewport edge point at nothing. A menu whose trigger scrolled away stays pinned at the window edge, Context menu is placed once and never follows, and text direction is re-read on every placement.
items.change: The arrow follows the trigger's centre, clamped clear of the corner. When the trigger scrolls out of view, tooltips and hover cards close and menus mark themselves; Context menu closes on scroll and resize; direction and paddings are read once per open; and CSS anchor positioning is used where it is supported.
items.why: An arrow points at what it belongs to, and a surface leaves with its anchor. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Side detection in script stays for engines without anchor positioning.

items.title: Dialog, Drawer and Command palette behave alike
items.what: Command palette closes on any click on the dialog itself (so a selection dragged out of the field closes it) and does not lock scrolling; locking the page without a stable gutter shifts it; Dialog and Drawer open with focus on the close button; and the palette's shortcut listener re-subscribes on every render and fires while typing.
items.change: One modal rule and one modal hook: scroll lock with a stable gutter, closing only when the press began on the backdrop, and exits that wait for their animation. First focus goes to an autofocus element, else the body's first control, else the least destructive footer action, else the surface, never the close; the palette's shortcut ignores repeats and waits while another modal is open.
items.why: Modals share one behaviour. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Whether a confirmation closes on a backdrop press
items.what: Confirm dialog closes when the backdrop is pressed, as its own documentation says. The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices and the libraries read never close an alert dialog on an outside press.
items.change: The owner decides. To change it, Dialog gains an option to ignore the backdrop (on by default) and Confirm dialog turns it off; the native closing attribute can replace it later.
items.why: A destructive confirmation should not be cancelled by a stray click.

options.label: Close only by its buttons or Escape
options.detail: A stray click no longer cancels a destructive confirmation without notice, as the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices advise.

options.label: Keep the backdrop close
options.detail: The documented behaviour, and forgiving.

items.title: Focus is never dropped
items.what: Tabbing from a Hover card's trigger into its first link closes the card. Dismissing a Toast, Chip, Tag, Attachment, Alert or Prompt suggestion drops focus to the page, and every Scroll area is an empty Tab stop when its content fits.
items.change: Hover card closes on blur only when focus leaves both trigger and card, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. A control that removes itself hands focus on (to the next toast, a neighbouring chip or tag, or the group) through one shared helper, and a Scroll area is a Tab stop only while it overflows.
items.why: Keyboard users never lose their place. Confirmed in source.

items.title: How long a tooltip waits
items.what: Tooltips open after 500 ms, with a 300 ms window in which the next one opens at once, close at once, and do not close on scroll. The desktop apps measured open in 150–300 ms (most often 300); the component libraries read wait 500–1500 ms.
items.change: The owner picks the first delay, and whether a tooltip that names an icon-only control opens sooner than a descriptive one. In every option, tooltips close on any scroll and use the native hint popover where it fits.
items.why: The desktop apps are faster than the libraries, and the skip window already makes scanning fast.

options.label: 300 ms for every tooltip
options.detail: What both closest desktop apps use; the skip window already makes scanning fast.

options.label: 150 ms for names, 500 ms for descriptions
options.detail: Faster for icon labels, but two delays to explain.

options.label: Keep 500 ms
options.detail: The component libraries' consensus.

items.title: Timing constants in one place
items.what: Delays are literals scattered through components: tooltips 500 / 300 / 0 ms, Hover card 700 / 300 ms, typeahead 1000 or 500 ms, Scroll area 600 ms, Video player 2000 ms, key repeat 400 / 60 ms, toasts 5000 ms and Splitter's 300 ms in CSS. The loading delay has no minimum visible time, so a load that finishes at 320 ms flashes a spinner for 20 ms.
items.change: One timing module exports every constant, the motion guide gains a timing table, and components import instead of writing literals. Button loading, Spinner and Skeleton show for at least 400 ms once they appear.
items.why: A delay is a system value, set once. Confirmed in source.

items.title: Runtime performance
items.what: Scroll area does layout reads on every scroll event inside every menu and drawer, Tabs and Segmented re-measure on every parent render, and Splitter and Panel commit every pointer move (Color picker and Property list too). No row is memoised and no list is windowed, so Tree view re-renders every row on focus and grouping in Combobox and Custom select grows with the square of the list; Splitter's Escape cannot cancel a pointer drag.
items.change: Scroll handlers run once per frame, measuring runs only when values change, drags batch moves per frame, cancel on Escape and offer a commit callback, and rows are memoised. Long lists skip off-screen rendering first, then gain opt-in windowing in List box, Tree view, Custom select, Combobox and Command palette that keeps accessibility intact.
items.why: Every menu and list should stay smooth at any length. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Windowing must keep accessible list semantics, so skipping off-screen rendering ships first.

items.title: Smaller stylesheets and an import with no side effects
items.what: The published stylesheet is 3,376,156 bytes unminified (518,880 gzipped) in one file: 1.63 MB of every setting preset and 1.22 MB of components with comments. The build parses it but writes the unminified source, and importing the React package installs window listeners although it is marked free of side effects.
items.change: The build writes minified output, apps that pin a theme can import per-component and per-setting stylesheets, and overlay listeners install on the first tooltip.
items.why: A library should ship minified and load only what it uses. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Source maps stay.

items.title: Behaviour fixes in single families
items.what: Enter on a Splitter evens the panes, where WAI-ARIA uses it to collapse one; Video player uses raw range inputs with their own styles; Dialog sets its scrolled header from a script.
items.change: Splitter's Enter collapses and restores where a pane can collapse (double-click still evens), Video player's seek and volume use Area's Slider, and Dialog's scrolled header comes from CSS scroll state where that removes a re-render.
items.why: Each family uses the standard key and Area's own parts. Medium confidence.
items.risk: Splitter's Enter changes a documented key.

items.title: Navigation and tabs round
items.what: A closable current Nav tab hugs its label, so its close covers 18 px of the name. Plate Tabs start their plate at the panel edge, so labels sit 10 px right of the body text while underline Tabs and Nav line up. List box's grid heading sits 10 px in over cells at 0 px with 34 px dead at the end, and Token row's soft style has a darker edge than Outline.
items.change: A closable tab is at least its label, gap and close wide (about 22 px wider when current), plate Tabs hang their plate so the first label sits on the content column, the grid heading sits on the cell edge and the grid fills its width, and Token row's two edges swap.
items.why: A revealed control never covers text that would fit, a strip's first label sits on the column, and outline is the stronger edge. Seen in the render.
items.risk: The plate hang needs the owner's glance.

items.title: Content and data round
items.what: Design card's held design overflows its ground and Asset card's group mosaic shrinks type to 7 px; Chart's last tick is cut (“Nov 7” to “Nov”); Table's sticky first column wraps (rows 59 px against 39), its header is 400 on a band and a fixed table splits code. Accordion's plain title equals its body, its variants default to different sizes and point the chevron opposite ways; Folder, File page and File image are faint (folders near-black in dark); and Skeleton draws every shape at a 4 px corner with text bars as tall as the font (a 52 px slab for Display).
items.change: Designs scale to fit both axes, chart text stays inside its frame, scrolling table cells do not wrap and a sticky column takes its content width, code never breaks in a table, Accordion has one 500 title, one default size and down for open, artwork edges reach the control edge in both themes, and skeleton bars are about the cap height with a small corner. A 500 muted table header, an 18 px body line and a frameless table go to the owner as proposals.
items.why: Each is a defect against a stated rule. Seen in the render.
items.risk: The frameless table is a new layout value, so it goes through intake.

items.title: Conversation round
items.what: Code block numbers a wrapped line at its middle and its filename aligns to neither column; Turn notice collapses to 75 px and wraps; Composer's footer note is centred, its footer buttons square under pill headers, its + glyph 2 px off, and the one-line composer pairs circles with a 19 px corner. Composer menu is 278 px beside a 280 px composer with a 14 px corner against 19; Empty state's ghost action reads as text; an answered Approval still says “Esc to cancel”; Message shows six actions while streaming; and Attachment's card is 160 × 64 px with 18 px empty and “PDF” twice.
items.change: Code numbers align to the first line, Turn notice is full width on one line, the composer's parts share its glyph column and pills, the menu over it takes its width with an 8 px group gap, an empty state's single action is outline (solid when primary), answered states drop their hint, message actions hide while streaming, and attachments are content height with a meta line. Code at 12 px and the one-line composer's shape are owner checks.
items.why: Each is a defect against a stated rule. Seen in the render.
items.risk: The composer's shape and the code size need the owner's glance.

items.title: Fields and pickers round
items.what: Date picker's panel has three left edges (input text 20 px in, the grid 12 px, “Clear” 14 px), Color field writes “#8D4DF3” in one layout and “8D4DF3” in another, Time field's empty colon is in the default ink between muted dashes, and Tag picker's wrapped rows are 5 px apart against 6 px columns.
items.change: “Clear” moves to the 12 px column, the hex value has one format, the colon follows the placeholder ink while empty, and Tag picker's rows gain 1 px.
items.why: A panel's content shares one column and a value keeps one format. Seen in the render.

items.title: Writing and content decisions carried over
items.what: Four earlier questions are still open: the toast, truncation-tooltip and reduced-motion rules where a published system's guidance differs from Area's, Reference list's em dash against the writing guide, and Description list's 160 px term column. Area's rules have not changed.
items.change: The owner decides each, and the result is recorded.
items.why: Nothing in this evaluation argues for changing Area's rules.

options.label: Keep Area's rules and record the differences
options.detail: Nothing in this evaluation argues for a change.

options.label: Adopt the other system's rules
options.detail: As the 2026-11-07 audit suggested.

items.title: An app shell composition
items.what: There is no app shell: the file named for one holds only Titlebar and Section heading, and every product recreation rebuilt the shell by hand. Titlebar has only content and an end slot, Panel's bar a title and one action with no centre, Nav items have no description line, and Panel stops at 500 px wide by default.
items.change: A layout component built only from Titlebar, Panel, Splitter and Nav: regions with default, minimum and maximum sizes, a collapse order, a layered mode, room for the window controls, a pane header with start, centre and end, and an account row as a Nav item slot with a description line. Panel's width cap defaults to none.
items.why: A composition is the lowest rung that ends the rebuilding; all four product recreations needed it.
items.risk: It goes through intake as a composition, with no new tokens.

items.title: A thread composition
items.what: Message and Composer exist, but the column around them is rewritten every time, and the transcript's gaps run 24, 24, 16, 2, 4, 10, 8, 20, 8, 7 and 24 px, so a reply sits as far from its question as from the next turn. Message has no attachments, heading, edited or branch state, Composer has no over-limit state, its send button cannot be replaced, and there is one face for reading.
items.change: A thread composition: a centred column with turn spacing (joined parts 2 px, meta 4 px, an attached part 8 px, a reply a step closer to its question than turns are to each other, for example 16 and 32 px), a docked composer with a fade, Message headings and attachments, an edited marker and branch switcher, and a replaceable send button with an over-limit state.
items.why: Every chat screen needs the same column, so it is built once. Medium confidence: the references give gaps between turns only.
items.risk: The question-to-reply gap needs the owner's eye.

items.title: Grid, shelf and a compact reference row
items.what: Asset grid and File grid are list boxes for selection, not layouts; Card's carousel has no paging arrows; Card's thumbnail is 84 px and Asset row 56 px with nothing in between; and the app still owns the two-dimensional grid keys.
items.change: A Grid that sets columns from a minimum card width (beside Stack), a Shelf with paging, and a 32 px compact row as a Card size or a small Asset row, through intake. The grid keys move out of app code.
items.why: Card grids and shelves are common product layouts, and none exists as a composition. Medium confidence.
items.risk: The compact row is a new size.

items.title: Product compositions that are still missing
items.what: None of these exists: notification history, a find bar, a status bar, a comment thread, a form validation summary, a rating pair, document blocks (callout, quote, to-do, toggle, page icon), marketing hero, navigation, footer and pricing, and a terminal or log view. The list of later candidates has aged, and four of them each serve three or more product types.
items.change: Each is proposed as a composition of existing families first (for example a find bar from Input, Toolbar and Count), in order of how many product types it serves, and started only when the owner asks.
items.why: Compositions come before new components. Medium confidence; not needed now.
items.risk: Each needs the owner's request before it starts.

items.title: Page and dashboard recipes
items.what: Tabs take the control height (30 px medium, 38 px large), while the products measured set page tab bars at 40–50 px. The feed recipe uses a 32 px margin, 12 px between cards and 48 px between sections, against one dashboard measured at 24, 16 and 24 px.
items.change: Recipes, not new sizes: page-level underline Tabs under a Page header use the large size plus the cluster gap above and below (46 px), panel Tabs stay medium, and a dashboard recipe (24 px margin, 16 px cards, 24–32 px sections) sits beside the feed recipe.
items.why: Page tabs and dashboards are composed from existing sizes. Medium confidence: two products measured.
items.risk: Nothing changes in the components.

items.title: Responsive behaviour, the mobile shell and touch gestures
items.what: No family responds to the viewport, nothing reads the screen's safe areas, mobile is the least covered product type (12 missing needs), and there is no swipe or long press.
items.change: Container-query rules per family first, with one breakpoint pair in tokens for the shell only. Safe-area insets on the shell, a bottom horizontal Nav, a floating Button, Drawer stops and a grabber, one swipe-to-dismiss for Toast and Drawer (40 px or 0.4 px per ms, cancelled by a 10 px reverse), and a 500 ms, 10 px long press for Context menu, each through intake.
items.why: Mobile and touch need system rules before any family can serve them. Medium confidence; not needed now.
items.risk: It is a system-wide convention, the sixth rung of the intake ladder.

items.title: Scroll edge fades
items.what: Only Nav, Tree view and Code fade content where it scrolls under an edge. The products measured fade 16–32 px, driven by scroll.
items.change: Scroll area gains a fade, on by default in menus, dialogs and panel lists: a 28–32 px eased mask only on the side with more content, with scroll padding equal to the padding plus the fade so focus never lands under it.
items.why: A fade shows there is more content without a rule. Strong evidence from three products.
items.risk: The mask colour must follow each ground.

items.title: A state for an inactive window
items.what: Nothing reacts when the window loses focus. One desktop app measured greys its primary buttons and drops its sidebar and header inks to 50% and 35%.
items.change: One hook quiets the solid action and the shell's inks when the window is inactive, and the desktop app sets it.
items.why: A desktop window shows when it is not the active one.
items.risk: It is the second rung of the intake ladder, a setting-level hook.

items.title: Drag and drop
items.what: Board has no drag, and Property list holds the system's only reorder.
items.change: Property list's reorder becomes a shared hook (keyboard pick, move, drop and cancel, pointer after 3–5 px, autoscroll within 20 px of an edge, announcements, and a “Move to…” alternative without dragging) for Board cards, Tabs and Tree view, Board first.
items.why: Reordering is one behaviour, written once with its keyboard and announcement. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: Board's drag is app code today.

items.title: A system's second and third colours become visible
items.what: The second and third brand colours and their text and on-colour roles, and eight support on-colours, are emitted but read by nothing and missing from the parked list. Some spacing, icon, display and layer tokens are also unused or unlisted.
items.change: The second colour gets a target (links, a chart's first series, badges, selection), and every token nothing reads is listed as parked with the job it waits for.
items.why: Every public token has a use or is listed as parked. Confirmed in source.
items.risk: The accent names are renamed first, with the third text ink.

items.title: Customization still missing
items.what: Area has 63 settings in 9 groups, but the typeface is fixed, there are two weights, titles stop at 26 px, height follows type, there are six code colour roles, Contrast only rises, colours stay in sRGB on wide-gamut screens and Field only stacks.
items.change: Each gap becomes a value on an existing setting or a small new setting, in rank order: typeface, weights, ramp, control height, second colour, icon weight, region separation, tracking and leading, layout spacing, motion per intent, overlay material, line style, syntax colours, chart hues, and the rest. No named looks, no options removed, and per-family corners stay out.
items.why: The owner wants every viable detail to be a choice. Medium confidence on the order; not needed now.
items.risk: Every new setting goes through the foundation-change skill and the settings' independence test.

items.title: Pill shapes add side room
items.what: Only fields clear part of a rounded corner; pill Buttons and Chips keep a rectangle's sides, so their text crowds the curve.
items.change: A shape whose corner passes 3/8 of its height adds the difference to its sides, rounded: 0 px at the default, 2 px at Corner 14 and 4 px on a 32 px pill. Soft Badge is excluded.
items.why: Text in a pill needs extra side room to look centred; one published system writes this rule.
items.risk: Pill widths grow by up to 4 px.

items.title: Smoother corners
items.what: Area has no smooth corner shape, and the earlier components audit left the question open.
items.change: The owner decides whether Corner gains a shape value (round or smooth) with a radius compensation, so a smooth curve reads the same size as a round one.
items.why: One product measured uses smooth corners with every radius multiplied by 1.25.

options.label: Add it as a setting value, round by default
options.detail: Keeps every option, and the desktop app's browser engine supports it.

options.label: Not now
options.detail: The concentric arithmetic would need the compensation everywhere.

items.title: Toast stack, limit, progress and several actions
items.what: Toasts list 8 px apart with no limit and no progress, and their reflow is animated by hand.
items.change: A variant, not a new default: a limit (3 by default) with older toasts collapsed behind (14 px up and 4% smaller per step) that expand on hover or focus, a progress option, and reflow by view transitions where that removes the hand animation.
items.why: Stacked toasts are common in shipped products, but the look is taste. Medium confidence; not needed now.
items.risk: The stacking look is taste.

items.title: Variants, slots and families the reviews named
items.what: Many requests are open: document tabs and an editor tab strip, split Diff with per-change actions, a floating outline, lazy Tree branches, an image viewer, calendar views, peek, a Gantt timeline, a data grid, input masks, an audio player, a selection frame, Table add and footer rows, icons in Breadcrumb and Tabs, width hooks, a Text and Heading component, and the listed component candidates.
items.change: Each goes through the intake ladder (nothing new, a setting, a composition, a slot, a value, an axis, a component) as its own proposal, ranked, and none is started unasked.
items.why: The library grows without duplicates only through intake. Medium confidence; not needed now.
items.risk: Each must pass intake, so the library does not bloat.

items.title: Gaps the app audit recorded
items.what: The app audit recorded five gaps that are not built: a row whose end holds a button form, an icon-only Copy button with no tooltip, a Popover's icon trigger that cannot take a tooltip, plain table cells mixed with TableCell, and a card for flow nodes.
items.change: Copy button and the Popover trigger gain a name tooltip as fixes, tested in the browser suites. The row slot, the TableCell rule and the flow node card go through intake as proposals, since they may be compositions only.
items.why: Every icon-only control has a name tooltip; the two missing ones are accessible-name defects. Read from the app audit.

notVerified: No hover, focus, pressed or open-overlay state was driven, in Area or in any live product; only the demos' forced states were rendered, and every behaviour finding is read from code, not reproduced.

The rendered capture set predates the light Layer contrast default of 50, so every light ground, plate, well and region-depth value was measured at Layers 0 and must be measured again after the merge.
The capture set itself is gone, because the session's scratch space was cleared; it must be regenerated from scripts in the repository.
The captures were rendered in a headless browser whose engine is newer than the desktop app's.
Several kinds of live product were never opened: a payments product, a launcher, a dashboard product and a storefront. Of those measured, one was seen in dark only and three in light only.
The desktop apps' values are read from their app bundles, not rendered, except one design tool's inspector captured on 2026-09-28; no desktop app was launched.
Forced colours, a screen reader, touch, right-to-left and zoom were never run, and target sizes at Compact were computed, not hit-tested.

Rendered centring offsets assume the typeface's ascent from Button's trimmed box (accurate to about 0.1 px); chart text drawn in SVG, numeric figure settings and text inside native inputs were not measured, and Video player's measures disagreed with its picture.
Whether truncated lines clip their descenders was not checked in the render.
